newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ONGC to start deep sea drilling.
newsitem.headline: India's ONGC to start deep sea drilling.

text.p: Indian state-run oil exploration company Oil and Natural Gas Corp Ltd (ONGC) will venture into deep sea exploration, a company spokeswoman said on Thursday.
"One of our rigs is being refitted for deep sea drilling, and we have identified the areas to target," public relations manager Ranjana Bhattacharya said.
The company will be drilling in the Krishna-Godavari and Cauvery basins in the Bay of Bengal, and the Kerala-Konkan and Kutch basins in the Arabian Sea, she said.
ONGC has also ventured into exploration for coal bed methane, a company statement said.

Bhattacharya said one well had been drilled in Durgapur in central India but was abandoned due to poor yields. Another well is currently being drilled and is expected to start production by mid-August.

The statement said ONGC was still awaiting government approval of its paraxylene plant in Gujarat. It is also awaiting approval of a liquefied natural gas (LNG) project for the importation and supply of LNG to bulk consumers. ONGC is one of the partners in the project.
The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted ONGC chairman Bikash Bora as saying the company would face liquidity problems if its outstandings with oil companies were not cleared within six months.

The news agency quoted him as saying that oil companies owed ONGC 17 billion rupees ($475 million). He was quoted as saying that this was not creating any immediate problems, but six months down the line it would affect operations. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
